steps.name: Walking skeleton: super-admin provisions an isolated workspace from the browser
criteria: A signed-in instance super-admin who submits the web provision form for a named workspace with a first-admin email causes a new workspace to be created via the shipped provision_workspace use-case.
The newly created workspace exists in Postgres and is isolated: it contains none of any other workspace's data.
The rendered web response reports the new workspace identifier and a first-admin invite link (the link is informational per D5; no sign-in via it is asserted).
The vertical wires end-to-end through the production session and double-submit CSRF layers to the shipped use-case and back to a rendered htmx success fragment.
The new instance_admin file stem is added to the LAYER-1e is_tenant_scoping_allowlisted allow-list (D6); cargo xtask check-arch and the foundry-acceptance suite stay green.
steps.scenario_name: A super-admin provisions a new isolated workspace from the browser

steps.name: Instance dashboard lists workspaces and offers provision and grant forms
criteria: A signed-in instance super-admin who opens the instance dashboard route receives a full HTML page (no-JS entry point).
The dashboard lists the existing workspaces.
The dashboard presents both a provision-workspace form and a grant-super-admin form, each carrying a valid CSRF token field.
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: The instance dashboard shows the workspace list and the provision and grant forms

steps.name: Super-admin grants super-admin to another operator from the browser
criteria: A signed-in instance super-admin who submits the grant form for an existing non-super-admin member causes that user to be granted super-admin via the shipped grant_instance_admin path.
The web response confirms the grant.
The granted user is afterwards an instance super-admin (is_instance_admin holds for that user).
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: A super-admin grants super-admin to another operator from the browser

steps.name: Granting super-admin twice from the browser is idempotent
criteria: A signed-in instance super-admin who submits the grant form for the same existing member twice receives a grant confirmation both times.
After two grants the target user is recorded as a super-admin exactly once (the role table holds no duplicate).
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: Granting super-admin twice from the browser is idempotent

steps.name: Grant form is not a user-enumeration oracle
criteria: A signed-in super-admin who submits the grant form for a known existing email and then for an email belonging to no user receives two responses that are confirmed identically.
Neither response reveals whether the submitted email belongs to a real user (no enumeration oracle distinguishes the known-email response from the unknown-email response in status or body).
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: Granting an unknown email does not reveal whether the user exists

steps.name: Signed-out admin-surface request refused like a never-existed path
criteria: A signed-out caller's request to each /admin/instance route (the GET dashboard and both POST routes) is refused.
Each refusal is byte-identical (status and full body) to a never-existed path's response; no 403, 401, or login redirect appears.
Nothing in the responses reveals that the admin surface exists.
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: A signed-out request to the admin surface is refused like a path that never existed

steps.name: Signed-in non-super-admin request to the admin surface is refused non-enumerably
criteria: A signed-in ordinary member (not a super-admin) who requests each /admin/instance route is refused.
Each refusal is byte-identical (status and full body) to the response for a path that never existed.
The non-super-admin refusal is byte-identical to the signed-out refusal for the same route, so the cause of refusal is indistinguishable.
Nothing in the responses reveals that the admin surface exists, and removing the gate would re-RED the byte-identity assertion (revert-reds-it litmus).
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: A signed-in non-super-admin request to the admin surface is refused non-enumerably

steps.name: Provision request without a valid security token is refused
criteria: A signed-in super-admin who submits the provision POST without a valid double-submit CSRF token is refused by the shipped csrf_middleware.
No new workspace is created as a result of the token-less request (the workspace set is unchanged).
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: A provision request without a valid security token is refused

steps.name: Legacy create-workspace route no longer exists
criteria: A POST to the legacy /workspaces create-workspace path is refused as a path that never existed (the route is deleted, not left inert, per D3).
The legacy path does not answer with the old 409 conflict response.
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: The legacy create-workspace route no longer exists

steps.name: Provisioning from the browser leaves existing workspaces untouched
criteria: Given a recorded snapshot of an existing workspace, provisioning a new workspace from the browser leaves that workspace and all its data and members byte-for-byte unchanged.
The newly provisioned workspace starts empty and isolated from the existing workspace.
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: Provisioning from the browser leaves existing workspaces untouched

steps.name: Browser-provisioned workspace is a real isolated tenant
criteria: Given a browser-provisioned workspace whose first admin holds issues in it, when she lists issues through the shipped resolve_active_workspace membership seam (D5) she sees only that workspace's issues.
No data belonging to any other existing workspace appears in her listing.
cargo xtask check-arch passes and the foundry-acceptance suite remains green.
steps.scenario_name: The browser-provisioned workspace is a real isolated tenant
